items.title: Are You Planning 20,000 AI Agents? Capital One Has a Warning | Abhijit Bose
items.summary: Most enterprises are still trying to figure out how to get a handful of AI agents into production. Capital One is running tens of thousands. Abhijit Bose, Senior VP and leader of the company's AI/ML platform engineering organization, joins Craig Smith to explain how a decade-old bet on the cloud - made when the economics didn't yet make obvious sense - became the foundation for everything Capital One is doing in AI today, from proprietary GPU clusters built in a single quarter to a platform that took model deployment from months down to about a week. The conversation gets concrete fast: a 24/7 AI concierge now running across car dealership websites, a generative AI system serving all 20,000-plus of Capital One's call center agents - adopted so successfully that agents started asking to be enrolled - and the Macau framework, Capital One's answer to the governance problem that's keeping most regulated industries from putting agentic AI into production. Bose's closing argument is the one that should worry every enterprise still in pilot mode: deploying five agents is manageable without a platform. Deploying 20,000 is a different problem entirely, and the companies that didn't start building the foundation years ago are going to find that out the hard way. Subscribe to Eye on A.I. for weekly conversations with the people building and deploying the future of AI.

items.title: How Storage Throughput Determines AI Workflow Outcomes - with Cameron Bahar of Everpure
items.summary: Scaling AI infrastructure from a single rack to hundreds introduces failure points that most enterprise storage systems were never designed to survive. In this episode, Cameron Bahar, GM of Scale AI at Everpure, breaks down what it actually takes to operate AI storage at scale, from cabling and telemetry to the operations overhead of keeping thousands of GPUs running. The conversation covers the operational burden of scale, why visibility and automation matter as deployments grow, and how companies across NeoClouds, financial trading, and autonomous vehicle development are navigating similar growing pains. items.title: Interview #107 Helen Gu, Founder & CEO, InsightFinder AI
items.summary: Helen Gu, Founder & CEO at InsightFinder AI, breaks down why most AI agent failures are silent: no error code, every dashboard green, just a confident wrong answer. She explains why read-only access is mostly safe while any write access needs guardrails and a human who stays accountable, how one mistake travels down a chain of agents from a misrouted task or a corrupted upstream price, and why debugging multi-agent systems echoes the move from mainframes to distributed systems. Helen also dives into why you can't use ChatGPT to grade ChatGPT, how runaway token use and rising latency expose agents stuck in loops long before anything errors, and how teams can catch a vendor's model update by watching the distribution of outputs shift. Finally, she shares why AI agents, like distributed systems, can never be proven 100% reliable, and why the monitoring should be done by other agents.
